name: Applied Artificial Intelligence
overview: You start with programming in C, linear algebra, calculus and statistics, then move into machine learning, deep learning, image recognition, language processing, robots and automatic control, using tools such as TensorFlow, Keras, PyTorch and SolidWorks. Laboratory work runs through the whole degree, and a semester-long internship in an industrial setting feeds into a two-semester final project in which you design, test and prototype an AI system. Applications range from automated manufacturing and autonomous transport to smart cities. Graduates work at technology and electronics manufacturers, research centres and public bodies, or continue to master's programmes such as Management of Artificial Intelligence Solutions.

name: Artificial Intelligence Systems
overview: After a foundation of mathematics, programming in C and Python, algorithms and databases, you study machine learning, software engineering, big data processing, cloud computing and image recognition. In the fifth semester you choose between two tracks: electronic systems, with microcontrollers and signal processing, or software systems, with deep learning and natural language processing. Lab work and integrated design projects run throughout, a semester-long company internship comes in year four, and the degree ends with a bachelor thesis. Graduates become machine-learning, deep-learning or computer-vision engineers, big data architects or analytics developers, and can go on to doctoral study.

name: Computer Engineering
overview: The first years combine physics, linear algebra and calculus with programming in C and Python, then electronics, computer logic, computer architecture and signals and circuits. From the fifth semester you follow either computer systems, covering cloud computing, networks and security, or embedded systems and programming, centred on microcontrollers and FPGA. Teaching is lab-heavy, with a practicum in circuit assembly and printed circuit board design, individual FPGA projects, a semester-long internship with a company that designs or services computer systems, and a bachelor thesis. Graduates go into technology firms and IT departments in finance and government, or on to master's study in electronics.

name: Information Technologies
overview: The study modules cover corporate IT management, process automation, cloud computing, data centres and the integration of financial information systems, with a specialisation in managing information technologies and security. Teaching is built around laboratory work, problem-based learning and course projects in programming techniques and software development. A 160-hour internship in the final year gives enterprise experience, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work as business analysts, systems engineers, UX/UI designers, project managers or software developers, and can continue to master's programmes such as Cyber Security Management or Data Science and Statistics.

name: Mathematics of Modern Technologies
overview: The degree centres on statistics and computer science for big data. You begin with calculus, discrete mathematics, linear algebra and C++, then move to probability, algorithms, databases, numerical methods, actuarial mathematics and neural networks. Core modules include machine learning, big data and data modelling. Teaching mixes laboratory work, problem-based learning and software such as Matlab and Python; the final year brings a complex project, an eight-week internship and a two-stage thesis. Electives include cryptography, image processing, quantum computing and financial engineering. Graduates become business analysts, software engineers or programmers, or go on to master's study in data science or AI.

name: Multimedia Design
overview: You combine creative and technical work: media production, computer graphics, web programming, game development, animation, audio technologies, image processing, augmented reality and human-computer interaction. Lab sessions use Adobe Premiere, Blender, Unity and similar tools, and course projects include games, websites and video, often in teams. A professional internship and a two-part bachelor thesis finish the degree. An enhanced study group follows a 2+1+1 route with a third year at Goldsmiths, University of London, leading to two bachelor's degrees. Graduates work in interactive media, design studios, advertising and cultural organisations, or continue to master's study such as Digital Graphics and Animation.

name: Bioengineering
overview: The first years build a base in mathematics, chemistry, physics and biology, followed by organic and physical chemistry, microbiology, biochemistry, and molecular and cell biology. Later modules cover chromatography, genetic engineering, bioinformatics, immunology and pharmaceutical biotechnology, with electives in environmental biotechnology. Teaching leans on laboratory sessions and course projects, a semester-long internship in a Lithuanian or foreign company, and a two-semester bachelor thesis with original research. Graduates are prepared for biotechnology, healthcare, food and agriculture research, bioenergy and quality-control laboratories, or for master's study such as Biomedical Engineering.

name: Mechanical Engineering
overview: You start with chemistry, physics, mathematics, engineering mechanics and materials science, then study mechanisms and machines, machine elements, mechanics of materials, CAD/CAE, cutting processes and 3D and laser manufacturing technologies. In the later years you choose one of three tracks: alternative energy equipment, environmental protection equipment, or machine design. Teaching combines labs and design course projects, an eight-week internship after the third year, and a two-semester bachelor thesis built around a prototype. Graduates work in machine design, production and assembly, energy organisations and research institutions, or start their own design and production firms, and can continue to doctoral study.

name: Mechatronics and Robotics
overview: After foundations in chemistry, physics, mathematics and engineering mechanics, you study mechanisms and machines, CAD/CAM/CAE, C++ programming, robotics, automatic control, digital automation and industrial logic controllers, ending with a design course for mechatronic and robotic systems. Laboratory work and several course projects run alongside, a semester-long internship takes place in factory settings, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work in production automation, robotic assembly lines, diagnostics and maintenance in industries such as pharmaceuticals, food and light manufacturing, or continue to master's study in mechatronics, automation or computer engineering.

name: Medical Engineering
overview: Mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering mechanics come first, followed by materials in medicine, biomechanics, human anatomy and physiology, and the design of medical, rehabilitation, orthopaedic and assistive devices and artificial organs. Later modules cover medical equipment, diagnostics, medical robots, rehabilitation technologies and medical psychology. You work in laboratories and on design projects, spend a semester in an internship with a company that designs or makes medical equipment, and complete a bachelor thesis involving research and design. Graduates work in hospitals, rehabilitation centres, medical device and orthopaedic companies, or go on to master's study such as Biomedical Engineering.

name: Automotive Engineering
overview: The first years cover mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering graphics and materials, then vehicle mechanics, internal combustion engines, vehicle dynamics, hydraulic and pneumatic systems and computer-aided engineering for transport machinery. Later you pick one of five specialisations: automotive transport, railway transport, automotive engineering, mobile machinery or autonomous vehicles. Laboratory work and design course projects run through the degree, and a semester-seven internship places you in a real enterprise. Graduates design vehicles and machinery, or work in transport operations, infrastructure bodies, charging networks and rescue services.

name: Aviation Mechanics Engineering
overview: After mathematics, physics, mechanics and engineering graphics, you study aircraft aerodynamics, structures, materials, functional systems, engines, instruments and flight dynamics. In the middle years you pick electives such as unmanned aerial vehicles, helicopter engineering or space technology. Teaching uses labs, course projects in aircraft design and finite element analysis, and a long internship in an airline maintenance setting, followed by a bachelor thesis. The curriculum is aligned with EASA Part 66 licensing requirements. Graduates work as aircraft technician-mechanics, design specialists or aviation safety regulators, or continue to master's study in aerospace engineering.

name: Civil Engineering
overview: You begin with mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering graphics, then materials science, mechanics of materials, building architecture and construction technology, before choosing one of three tracks: geotechnics, design of buildings and structures, or design of bridge structures. Core design subjects include reinforced concrete, steel structures, structural mechanics and foundation design. Teaching combines laboratory work in soil mechanics and materials testing, integrated design projects, BIM modelling and visits to construction sites. Graduates design and supervise buildings and structures, run construction processes, work in geotechnics or consulting, or start their own firms, and can continue to master's or doctoral study.

name: Environmental Technology
overview: The degree starts with environmental processes, calculus, hydrology and engineering graphics, then turns to pollution prevention, air quality, water supply network design, wastewater treatment, waste management and resource recovery, environmental biotechnology and climate change mitigation. Teaching includes laboratory testing, course projects in water and sewer design, field studies at treatment sites, GIS and pollution modelling, and internships with environmental companies. For the thesis you choose environmental protection technologies or water management. Graduates work in environmental institutions, waste and recycling firms, water utilities and consultancies, or continue to a master's.

name: Business Management
overview: The early semesters mix quantitative subjects (linear algebra, analysis, probability) with business fundamentals, business law and organisational behaviour, followed by e-business, micro- and macroeconomics, accounting, financial management, digital leadership and entrepreneurship. From the fifth semester you specialise in financial management, business project management or marketing. Case studies and projects focus on the needs of small and medium-sized enterprises, a semester-long internship takes place in Lithuanian or international firms, and a two-semester thesis closes the degree. Graduates work as project managers, marketing specialists, product managers, business analysts or consultants, or start businesses.

name: Financial Engineering
overview: A quantitative base of linear algebra, analysis, probability, statistics and Python supports courses in economics, corporate finance, management accounting, behavioural finance, econometrics and financial risk management, plus derivatives such as futures, options and swaps. Teaching combines lectures, seminars and lab work, with a research project, an investment project and a complex financial engineering project. A final-year internship in Lithuanian or foreign companies precedes the bachelor thesis, and an enhanced group can earn an international management accounting certificate. Graduates work in market analysis, forecasting and asset management, or continue to a master's in data science or economics engineering.

name: Creative Industries
overview: You study business communication, creative business, mass communication, media production and sociology, then media studies, research methods, public relations, visual communication, advertising and digital communication, with electives such as film industry, music industry or photography. Learning is project-based, with an integrated project, media projects, a final-semester internship and a bachelor thesis. Students may also work towards a concurrent Bachelor of Arts from Kiel University of Applied Sciences in Germany. Graduates go into advertising, design, film, music, publishing and games, communication agencies and cultural organisations, or work freelance.

name: Entertainment Producing
overview: You study business communication, the psychology of entertainment, mass communication, media production, digital image technology, marketing and public relations. From the fifth semester you choose entertainment communication, with live event scripting and directing and the music and film industries, or film communication, with script writing and film production management. An integrated project in the sixth semester turns a creative idea into a product, and research modules teach quantitative and qualitative methods. A double degree with Kiel University of Applied Sciences in Germany is offered. Graduates work as producers, event organisers, creative project managers, content creators and entertainment marketing specialists.

name: Architecture
overview: Design studios form the backbone of the five years, moving from architectural fundamentals, drawing, history and BIM to projects on community, technology, context, heritage and innovation. Alongside them you study theory and composition, urban form, GIS-based urban analysis, tectonics and heritage protection. Studio work uses sketches, computer models and scaled models, with intensive workshops on real briefs, field studies of heritage sites, a two-month internship in a design firm and a master thesis. Graduates work as independent architects, in private firms and in public planning and heritage bodies, and the degree is recognised for regulated practice in the EU.

name: Economics and Finance
overview: Over three years you study microeconomics, macroeconomics, statistics and mathematics, then international economics, econometrics, labour economics, public finance, investment and risk, and financial accounting, with research methods alongside. Teaching draws on practitioners from universities, NGOs and business, and on the faculty's behavioural economics laboratory. Internships are mostly with international companies in Lithuania and abroad, followed by a qualification practice and a bachelor thesis, and you can work towards an international CMA management accounting certificate. Graduates go into finance and strategy roles, public policy work and analytical units, or on to a master's.

name: Business Administration
overview: You study microeconomics, macroeconomics, management, finance, marketing and organisational behaviour, then financial reporting, human resources, business law, entrepreneurship, leadership and strategic management. Electives include digital marketing, sales management, lean management, logistics, artificial intelligence and e-sports. Business and public-sector representatives take part in lectures, and practical work comprises term papers, a qualification placement and a bachelor thesis. Graduates move into management, consulting and organisational administration, start their own ventures, or continue to a master's in business administration.

name: Logistics and Commerce
overview: After microeconomics, mathematics and business basics, you study logistics management, logistics equipment and technology, e-commerce, warehousing and inventory, transport systems, and customs procedures, with finance, human resources and business law as support. Entrepreneurship training, business planning and market research give practical experience, and the final year brings a professional internship and a bachelor thesis. Partner firms contribute lectures, company visits, traineeships and thesis topics. Graduates work as logistics coordinators, supply chain administrators and transport specialists, in retail and agricultural logistics, or start commerce ventures.

name: Sustainable Bio-Business Management
overview: Early semesters cover mathematics, economics, business law and management basics; later modules combine financial management and marketing with green chemistry, biomaterials, circular economy, agricultural systems, biotechnology and sustainable bioenergy. Two practicums, in semesters five and eight, give workplace training, and a bachelor thesis closes the degree. Partner companies give lectures and offer internships and project topics, and Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates work as managers, project managers, sustainability consultants and marketing or sales specialists in bioeconomy organisations, or in related ministries.

name: Political Studies: World Politics and Economy
overview: The degree joins political science with economics: political systems, global politics, international relations, international political economy, geopolitics, EU politics, human rights and economic diplomacy. Regional courses look at East Asia, Latin America, and US, Russian and EU policy, with attention to the EU's Eastern Partnership. Research methods run alongside, and internships take place at political institutions, international organisations, companies and diplomatic missions, before a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as policy advisers, diplomats and researchers, including in foreign ministries, or continue to a master's.

name: Political Studies: International Politics and Development Studies
overview: You study political systems, international relations, development studies, colonialism and post-colonialism, human rights, comparative politics, international economics and conflict resolution in developing countries. Regional courses focus on the post-Soviet states and the Middle East and North Africa, and you add a regional language at B1 level, chosen from French, Spanish, Arabic, Russian or Turkish. Internships take place in political institutions, international organisations and diplomatic missions, followed by a bachelor thesis. Graduates work in government, research institutes and international organisations, or go on to a political science master's.

name: Sociology and Anthropology: Society, Culture and Communication
overview: The degree pairs classical and contemporary sociological thinking with communication: public relations, strategic communication, visual communication and international communication. Topic courses cover religion, crime and social control, gender, ethnicity and nationalism, migration and family diversity, and you learn qualitative and quantitative methods. Practical work includes two in-service trainings, a creative production lab, an engaged journalism lab and a bachelor thesis, with Erasmus+ and bilateral exchanges available. Graduates work as analysts and communication specialists in media, advertising, market research, human rights organisations, think tanks and ministries.

name: English Philology
overview: You study English phonetics, linguistics, morphology and syntax alongside British, American and Canadian literature, translation strategies and language teaching methodology. Practical elements include career-planning training, translation practice, corpus analysis and a qualifying teaching practice. Electives cover semantics and pragmatics, sociolinguistics, literature and media, and American and British civilisation. The programme works with schools, translation agencies, language course providers and international companies. Graduates become translators, interpreters and English teachers, work in banks, businesses and EU organisations, or go on to master's and doctoral study.

name: Biology and Genetics
overview: You study general biology, physics and chemistry, then invertebrate and vertebrate biology, morphophysiology, microbiology, biochemistry, general and molecular genetics and immunology, and later biophysics, cell cultures, ecological genomics, epigenetics and neurobiology. Teaching includes laboratory courses, field work in plant and animal biology, term papers and a bachelor thesis, with internships chosen in companies and institutions linked to the programme. Electives range from beekeeping and forest entomology to aquaculture systems and ecogenotoxicology. Graduates work in biotechnology, biopharmaceutics, the food industry, environmental protection, health care and forensics, or continue to a master's or doctorate.

name: Biotechnology
overview: The first semesters cover general biology, chemistry, biotechnology and mathematics, then organic chemistry, physics and genetics, followed by biochemistry, immunology, cell cultures, enzymology, bioinformatics, omic technologies and AI in biotechnology. Teaching centres on laboratory work with modern equipment, two internship periods with partners such as Thermo Fisher Scientific, and a bachelor thesis. Partner companies help shape the curriculum and give guest lectures, and electives include fermentation technologies and food biotechnology. Graduates work in research laboratories, biopharmaceutical and food industries, cosmetics or environmental agencies, or continue to a master's.

name: Informatics Systems
overview: You start with mathematics, programming, discrete structures and object-oriented programming, then graphics and visualisation, computer architecture, databases, human-computer interaction, networks, Java, software engineering, internet technology and AI applications. From there you follow one of three tracks: software systems (mobile, IoT and cloud), artificial intelligence systems, or business informatics. Teaching combines labs, applied research with industry partners, term papers, a final-year practicum under a mentor and a bachelor thesis. Graduates work as software developers, architects, data analysts and project managers in start-ups and government, or continue to a master's in informatics or computer engineering.

name: Multimedia and Internet Technologies
overview: Mathematics, programming, databases, computer architecture and networks sit beside audiovisual art, visual communication, composition and digital sound. Later modules cover programming virtual environments and computer games, graphics and visualisation, augmented reality, AI in games, interactive multimedia and animation, and web graphics design. Teachers and students work with multimedia, creative-industry and game-development firms, and the final semester combines an internship with the bachelor thesis. Graduates work in game development, 3D modelling, animation, virtual reality, web design and creative technology, or continue to a master's in Lithuania or abroad.

name: Sustainable Engineering
overview: You begin with chemistry, mathematics, physics, engineering graphics, mechanics, biology and programming, then thermodynamics, electronics, agronomy, fluid mechanics, machine elements and computer-aided design. Later courses cover environmental engineering, mechatronic systems, AI and machine learning, robotics and drones in agriculture, bio-waste recovery, circular economy and data science. Teaching includes laboratories and a semester-long engineering design practice, and more than forty companies equip labs and contribute to courses. Graduates work as engineers, technologists and managers in agricultural modernisation, food production, waste management and bioenergy, or continue to a master's.

name: Music Production
overview: You study sound engineering, sound recording basics and technologies, sound recording design, applied music production, composition, and music marketing and project management, with a thread of audiovisual art linking sound to video, photography and graphic design. Teaching is project-based and uses three professional recording studios, with video and multimedia projects, a music production practice in the final semester and a bachelor thesis. The whole programme is taught in English. Graduates work as audio specialists, sound directors for television, radio and theatre, music producers, sound artists and managers in music organisations, or continue to study abroad.

name: Performing Arts
overview: Individual instrument or voice study sits beside ensemble work in chamber groups, orchestras, jazz ensembles and vocal groups through all eight semesters, with an opera studio, soloist practice and music event practice. Theory covers solfeggio, harmony, polyphony and composition, with music history from the Middle Ages to the 21st century and teaching methods for choirs. You choose one of eight tracks: accordion, choir conducting, jazz, piano, strings, vocal, wind and percussion, or popular music, and finish with a final art project in that track. Erasmus+ exchanges are available. Graduates perform in orchestras, ensembles, theatre and opera, teach, or continue to a master's.

name: Sports Studies (in Kaunas)
overview: The first year covers functional anatomy, motor control, sports genetics, biomechanics, physiology and medicine, and biochemistry and nutrition, followed by three levels of coaching theory and didactics and the theory and practice of a chosen sport, plus sports psychology and testing in sport, with attention to AI and e-sports. Coaching practice runs over three semesters, with internships in sports centres in Lithuania or abroad and a partnership with Kaunas Zalgiris basketball club. Optional tracks lead to international certificates, for example in athletic training or personal training. Research methods and a thesis finish the degree. Graduates work as coaches, athletic trainers, competition officials and sports managers.

name: Business and Finance
overview: Each semester is split into three modules, and teaching is built around real business challenges set by business experts rather than lectures alone. The emphasis falls on corporate finance: analysing cash flows, assessing investments, preparing budgets, choosing financing models, judging a company's financial position and its risks, and drafting development plans that secure funding. Graduates work as financial, investment, budget, treasury or risk analysts, accountants, banking officers and internal auditors in companies, banks, insurers, audit and consulting firms and the public sector, or start businesses.

name: International Business
overview: Each semester is split into three modules, and the subjects span marketing and sales, organisation and personnel management, accounting and finance, entrepreneurship, leadership, client relations, negotiation, business psychology, international protocol and economic analysis, plus setting up and winding up a company. Teaching is built around real business challenges, with project preparation, business communication and foreign languages alongside. Graduates work as international business, business development or operations managers, management consultants, project managers and trade specialists in finance, insurance, trade and marketing, and many start their own ventures.

name: Accounting and Audit
overview: The first years cover business mathematics, economic theory, fundamentals of accounting, financial accounting, management, statistics and marketing, then cost accounting, corporate finance, business law, tax accounting, financial statements and management audit. Later courses turn to financial audit, budgeting, public-sector accounting, accounting information systems and performance evaluation, with course work, a professional practice and a bachelor thesis. Paid internships with large firms such as PwC, EY, Deloitte and KPMG are common, and studies can be combined with work. Graduates become accountants, auditors, financial analysts and consultants, or continue to a master's.

name: Economics and Finance
overview: The degree rests on economics, finance and data analysis: corporate and public finance, financial markets, macroeconomics, statistics, econometrics and data visualisation, plus fintech technologies and their regulation. Lectures and seminars build argument and presentation skills, computer laboratories use statistical software and a Bloomberg terminal for live market data, and almost every course brings in guest speakers from economics or finance. Graduates work in banks, investment management, financial analysis, fintech, consulting, ministries, central banks and research institutes, as finance analysts, investment managers or business consultants.

name: Global Marketing
overview: The curriculum moves from foundations in management and marketing to applications across business sectors, the integration of sales, management and marketing, international marketing, and market research methods, with a group of individually chosen studies. You work with quantitative data, build advertising campaigns for digital and traditional media, and use AI tools for audience segmentation and campaign optimisation. Around eighty companies host students for professional internships each year, among them Danske Bank, Teltonika, Wolt, IKEA and DHL. Graduates work as sales managers, marketing experts, business managers and business developers.

name: Management
overview: You study strategic business development, organisational management, human resources, marketing and market research, accounting and financial management, and business negotiation. Lecturers use practical examples, and you can take part in integrated practical activities, including creating a start-up in the VU TechHub pre-accelerator. There are study branches, among them one on global business and analytics, and a double-degree route spends five to six semesters at the University of Granada in Spain, ending with degrees from both universities. Graduates work as sales managers, marketing experts, business managers or developers in business and the public sector, run their own businesses, or continue to a master's.

name: Quantitative Economics
overview: The three years run from core economic principles, mathematical methods and statistics to economic theory, econometrics and finance, with a capstone project and an internship in the final year. Teaching is delivered entirely in English by research-active faculty and leans on applied research with empirical evidence. A double-degree option with the Saint-Etienne School of Economics at Jean Monnet University in France is available. Graduates work as financial analysts, data analysts, economists and research analysts in financial services, research institutions, government and consulting, and the English-language degree supports applications to master's programmes abroad.

name: Bioinformatics
overview: Mathematics, computer science and the life sciences are taught side by side, with teachers from the Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics, the Life Sciences Center and research institutes. Early semesters cover biology, chemistry, discrete mathematics, programming and biochemistry; later ones cover genetics, molecular and cell biology, algorithms, statistics, databases, software engineering and several courses in bioinformatics itself. Laboratory and programming practicals run throughout, with project work and a final internship and bachelor thesis. Graduates work as bioinformatics software specialists in research laboratories, biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies and genetic research, or continue to a master's or doctorate.

name: Innovative Communication and Entrepreneurship
overview: The degree starts with core academic skills, entrepreneurship and networking technologies, moves to innovation and business model development, integrated communication and audience analysis, and ends with research methods, digital content creation, leadership and sustainable business development. Teaching is practical, with real projects and business tasks, an internship and a final thesis applied to an actual setting, in cooperation with outside organisations. Graduates work as communications specialists, digital content creators, brand managers, public relations and marketing specialists, innovation project managers or start-up founders, in agencies, start-ups, public institutions and international organisations.

name: Chemistry of Nanomaterials
overview: You begin with general chemistry, mathematics and physics, then analytical, physical, organic, inorganic and polymer chemistry, followed by biochemistry, quantum and colloid chemistry, spectroscopy and specialised nanochemistry subjects, with electives for deeper focus. Laboratory work and practical training are central, teaching you to make and analyse nanomaterials with modern instrumental methods and to work safely and in teams. Graduates work as materials and nanomaterials researchers, pharmaceutical nanotechnology researchers and quality control specialists in medicine, electronics, energy and environmental fields, or continue to a master's or doctorate.

name: Light Engineering
overview: The programme covers laser and semiconductor physics, optics, optoelectronics, digital modelling and smart lighting, on top of physics, chemistry, electronics and mathematics, including material synthesis, characterisation techniques and the principles of photovoltaic devices. Laboratory work on the university's growth and characterisation equipment is central, and students are encouraged to join research projects early. You can specialise deeply in an optoelectronics field or keep a broader base. Graduates work in light technology companies, with laser specialists and in research centres, helped by the strong Lithuanian laser industry, or continue to a master's or doctorate in laser physics, optics or materials science.

name: Politics of Global Challenges
overview: Political science theory sits beside social sciences, humanities and the science behind global problems in technology, environment and health, with qualitative, quantitative and digital research methods, big data analysis and data visualisation. Teaching is research-oriented: you formulate a research problem tied to a global challenge, plan it and carry out small-scale scientific or applied research, often working with people from other disciplines. Graduates work as policy analysts, strategic planning specialists, government analysts, programme officers in NGOs and international organisations, or climate policy specialists, or continue to a master's in social sciences, humanities or interdisciplinary studies.

name: Sustainability and Future Societies
overview: You apply sociology, social work, psychology, criminology, management, technology and AI to social sustainability problems, with advanced social research methods, demographic research, policy evaluation and project management for social innovation. Learning is applied, through project work, research and community-based initiatives, and working with communities, organisations and international partners. Graduates work as urban planners, sustainability officers and policy analysts in the public sector, as social innovation managers and impact assessors in NGOs, or as sustainability consultants and corporate responsibility leads in business.

name: English Philology
overview: You study how English is structured and used in society and culture, the literature of English-speaking countries and media analysis, while building communication skills at C1-C2 level through academic writing, creative and content writing, public speaking and translation. Digital resources support independent and group work, and you can add a minor in German philology, Spanish language and literature, or Scandinavian studies. Graduates work as teachers, translators, editors, publishers, journalists, content creators and business communication specialists in education, media and cultural institutions, or continue to a master's at home or abroad.

name: Business Data Analytics
overview: Over three years you combine statistics and machine learning with business management, economics and finance, learning to collect, analyse and interpret complex data and to frame business problems in mathematical and statistical terms. You build business data analytics projects with specialised software, applying theory to real problem-solving. The programme collaborates with VU Business School and the University of Minho's School of Economics, Management and Political Science. Graduates work as business, financial and economic data analysts, forecasters, customer behaviour analysts and builders of recommendation systems, in consulting, finance and research.

name: English and Another Foreign Language
overview: You study English to C1 level and German to B2, with a focus on the structure of both languages and how linguistic phenomena relate, alongside language and literature, knowledge of the ancient world and specialised modules, plus electives chosen to your interests. Teaching stresses practical, real-life language use across fields and builds teamwork, critical thinking and self-assessment. Graduates work in translation, interpreting, publishing, content creation, language teaching and customer service, in foreign institutions in Lithuania, embassies, international organisations, media and business, or continue to a master's.

name: English and Another Foreign Language
overview: You study English to C1 level and French to B2, with a focus on the structure of both languages and how linguistic phenomena relate, alongside language and literature, knowledge of the ancient world and specialised modules, plus electives chosen to your interests. Teaching stresses practical, real-life language use across fields and builds teamwork, critical thinking and self-assessment. Graduates work in translation, interpreting, publishing, content creation, language teaching and customer service, in foreign institutions in Lithuania, embassies, international organisations, media, finance and logistics, or continue to a master's.

name: English and Another Foreign Language
overview: You study English to C1 level and Spanish to B2, with a focus on the structure of both languages and how linguistic phenomena relate, alongside language and literature, knowledge of the ancient world and specialised modules. Learning options include semester exchanges through Erasmus+ at Spanish universities, internships built into the curriculum, and elective modules for a personal path. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, language specialists, content creators and teachers in embassies, international organisations, cultural institutions, media, publishing, finance and logistics, or freelance, or continue to a master's.

name: Spanish Philology
overview: You learn Spanish to a professional level (C1-C2) and analyse the language through phonetics, grammar, lexicology, pragmatics and language development, while studying the literature and cultures of Spain and Latin America with current methods of language and literature research. Optional topics include Spanish women's literature, Spanish art, contemporary theatre and the history of Spanish-speaking America. Graduates work as Spanish teachers, translators, interpreters, journalists, content creators and marketing or tourism professionals, in government, international organisations and embassies, or continue to a master's in arts, humanities or social sciences.

name: Lithuanian Studies
overview: You learn or improve Lithuanian to B2 level while studying Lithuanian culture, literature, history, and social and political life, with a look at the neighbouring Baltic countries. The degree develops research methods in linguistics and cultural studies, project skills and cross-cultural analysis, and can be combined with other fields such as management, communication or pedagogy for a personal path. Graduates work as language teachers, curriculum developers, cultural project managers, museum specialists, translators and policy analysts wherever intercultural competence and knowledge of Lithuania are needed.

name: Multilingualism and Digital Technologies
overview: You study English (up to C1-C2) and German (to B2) with comparative linguistics and the literature and cultures of both, alongside applied informatics: digital content creation, data management, web technologies, and language technology including natural language processing. The programme moves from foundations to more complex subjects and asks you to design digital solutions that suit their target audience, using modern IT and AI-based tools and working in multilingual teams. Graduates work as digital communication, language technology, localisation, web content and digital transformation specialists, or as junior software developers and project coordinators.

name: Central and East European Languages and Cultures
overview: This Polish Studies route is designed for beginners, taking you from first steps to advanced Polish alongside Polish literature and culture, the history of Central and Eastern Europe and modern methods of linguistic research. The coursework links language with analytical thinking and intercultural awareness for use in diplomacy, cultural mediation and international communication. Graduates work as international relations specialists, Polish teachers, editors and proofreaders, cultural project managers, researchers and freelance translators, in embassies, international organisations, cultural institutions, media and publishing.

name: Central and East European Languages and Cultures
overview: This Russian Studies route is designed for beginners and takes Russian to B2-C1 level alongside literature, cultural theory and linguistic analysis, set in the wider region with attention to its politics, history and media literacy. The structure is flexible: you can choose courses from politics, history, management or pedagogy, and study more than twenty languages. Teaching builds independent research and text analysis across styles and genres. Graduates work as international relations specialists, language educators, translators, editors, cultural project managers and researchers in media, publishing, diplomacy, government and international organisations, or continue to further study.

name: Scandinavian Studies
overview: You take Danish from the ground up to B2 level while studying the Nordic region more broadly: its welfare model, historical turning points, Viking-era heritage, mythology, media and popular culture, with options on endangered Nordic languages and cultures, Nordic music and the multicultural urban identities of young people. Learning is experience-based, and nearly half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices, including courses from other programmes. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, teachers, cultural specialists, researchers and media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies, or continue to humanities or social science master's study.

Graduates work as translators, interpreters, lecturers, teachers, cultural specialists, researchers, tourism specialists and media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies.

Shared humanities courses sit beside Scandinavian ones, and nearly half the curriculum is shaped by your own choices. Graduates work as translators, interpreters, teachers, cultural specialists, researchers, tourism specialists and media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies, and many go on to advanced humanities study.

Graduates work as translators, interpreters, teachers, lecturers, cultural specialists, researchers and tourism or media professionals, in embassies, international organisations and Nordic companies, or continue to humanities or social science study.

name: Nursing
overview: Lectures and seminars use clinical examples, case studies and problem-solving exercises, and clinical placements across all levels of the health service take you from observation to increasingly complex procedures under qualified supervision. You build skills in communication, ethics, health promotion, disease prevention, work organisation, leadership and medical information systems, and can take part in research at university clinics within interdisciplinary teams. Graduates work as general practice nurses in hospitals, outpatient and family practice, rehabilitation and long-term care, or independently under Lithuanian law, and can continue to a master's in Lithuania or abroad.

name: Medicine
overview: The degree builds the sciences medicine rests on, including human anatomy, physiology and pathology and scientific methodology, then moves into clinical disciplines, with practice in history-taking, physical examination, laboratory work, instrumental investigations and treatment planning. Clinical placements fill a large share of the later years, and students can take part in research and international exchange. Students who do not speak Lithuanian receive Lithuanian language teaching over six semesters, aimed at the level needed in clinical settings. Graduates go into residency and specialisation, hospital practice, public health, research or industry, and the degree supports mobility across Europe.

name: Dentistry
overview: You start with anatomy, physiology and biochemistry and move gradually into pre-clinical practice with simulated procedures, then into clinical placements where diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive dental work is done under supervision. Clinical intensity grows each year, and in the final semesters you manage your own patients from diagnosis to treatment planning. The curriculum follows EU standards for the profession and stresses professional ethics, communication and teamwork with other health professionals. Graduates work in private or public dental practice, set up their own practices, enter residency in fields such as orthodontics or oral surgery, or go into research, academia or industry.

name: Economics and Management
overview: You study economics, finance and financial management, marketing and consumer behaviour, statistics and econometrics, international economics, business analytics and risk management, plus themes such as the digital, environmental, urban and sharing economies. Teaching centres on data analysis and decision-making in management, investment and business financing, with independent learning, an internship and a bachelor thesis, and Erasmus exchange is possible. Graduates work as economists, project managers, finance specialists, business analysts, consultants or civil servants, in industrial and logistics companies and government agencies, or start their own ventures.

name: Information Systems and Cyber Security
overview: You learn programming, algorithms, databases and computer networks together with their security side, then operating systems, information security, ethical hacking, cryptography, digital crime investigation, virtualisation, AI fundamentals and cyber law. About half of the subjects are taught by practitioners, and you work on real information system development, testing and risk management, finishing with an internship and a thesis. Electives let you take AI and automation courses from any programme at the university. Graduates work as security specialists, analysts, architects, programmers, testers, database administrators and project managers, or in auditing and security management.

name: Language and Artificial Intelligence Management
overview: The degree joins English linguistics with information systems: semantics, pragmatics and discourse analysis, the analysis of natural and AI-generated language, writing and refining queries for generative AI, programming and data processing basics, how training data is built and checked, and the ethical and legal principles of AI-generated language. You learn to design, assess and improve how people interact with generative AI, to spot bias, manipulation and disinformation, and to reach C1 English. Graduates work as human-AI interaction specialists, content quality or discourse analysts, conversational systems and disinformation specialists, or AI policy specialists.

name: Marketing Technologies
overview: You combine traditional and digital marketing theory with information technology: e-marketing strategy, beginner-level programming, AI applications, mobile app development, data analytics and the digitisation of business models. Theory is paired with practice on real situations, including collecting, analysing and presenting marketing research data and hands-on work with AI tools, and Erasmus exchange is available. Graduates work as internet marketing and marketing technology specialists, website developers, information systems analysts, product and project managers, content managers and social media or PPC managers.

name: Economics and Investment
overview: The degree gives a broad base in economics, mathematics, management, finance, law, marketing and accounting, then two elective blocks, one in finance and investments and one in global economy. You learn to analyse economic situations at company, national and global level, assess resource use and company performance, support funding and investment decisions and take part in macroeconomic policy planning. Graduates work as economists, financial analysts and managers in public and private organisations, banks and businesses, forecasting economic indicators.

name: Software Engineering
overview: Following ACM guidelines, the degree joins software engineering with computer science: programming languages and frameworks, algorithms and data structures, databases, computer architecture, networks and operating systems, and the whole development lifecycle from requirements and design to testing and quality assurance. You choose between two branches, e-service systems for banks, insurers and the public sector, or robotic systems, covering robotic architectures and control software. Graduates work as systems analysts, architects, software developers, automation engineers, database administrators and testers in software firms and e-services, or continue to a master's.
